content: Electrolytes are minerals present in your blood and other bodily fluids that carry an electric charge. Maintaining a proper balance of electrolytes in your body is crucial because they play a significant role in regulating the amount of water in your body, the acidity (pH) of your blood, muscle contractions, and other essential physiological processes. When you sweat, your body loses electrolytes, and it is necessary to replenish them by consuming fluids. Electrolytes in the blood exist in the form of acids, bases, and salts, including substances such as sodium, calcium, potassium, chloride, magnesium, and bicarbonate. These electrolyte levels can be assessed through laboratory blood tests.
